_meta.scope: Conservative primary-study evidence matched to tracked supplements and medications.
_meta.inclusionRule: Every displayed statement must be directly supported by its cited primary study and must disclose the study model, exposure context, and main limitation.
_meta.legacyAudit: The previous 114-entry catalog was retired after an end-to-end PMID audit found review citations, unrelated papers, over-broad claims, and model-to-human extrapolation. Entries return only after claim-level verification.

evidence.summary: Muscle biopsies from 11 adults who developed weakness and lipid-storage myopathy while taking sertraline showed respiratory-chain deficiency.
evidence.model: 11 adults with muscle weakness and lipid-storage myopathy during sertraline treatment
evidence.exposure: Prescribed treatment; dose and duration are not reported in the PubMed abstract.
evidence.limitations: A selected case series can show an association, but not frequency, causality, or risk at this user's dose.
evidence.title: Lipid storage myopathy associated with sertraline treatment is an acquired mitochondrial disorder with respiratory chain deficiency.

evidence.summary: Five patients with linezolid-related hyperlactatemia had markedly reduced mitochondrial COX-II protein and COX activity; most abnormalities returned toward control after withdrawal and recovery.
evidence.model: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 5 patients during hyperlactatemia and after recovery
evidence.exposure: Long-term linezolid treatment followed by withdrawal.
evidence.limitations: Only patients who developed hyperlactatemia were studied; this does not estimate risk for all users.
evidence.title: Reversible inhibition of mitochondrial protein synthesis during linezolid-related hyperlactatemia.

evidence.summary: Doxycycline produced a mitonuclear protein imbalance, reduced maximal respiration, and fragmented mitochondria across cardiac cell and animal models.
evidence.model: H9C2 cells, adult rat cardiomyocytes, Drosophila, and mice
evidence.exposure: Experimental cell and animal exposures; equivalence to routine human dosing was not established.
evidence.limitations: No treated-human mitochondrial or clinical outcome was measured in this study.
evidence.title: The Antibiotic Doxycycline Impairs Cardiac Mitochondrial and Contractile Function.

evidence.summary: Amiodarone and its metabolite concentration-dependently impaired complex I- and II-supported respiration in human blood cells and a liver-derived cell line.
evidence.model: Human platelets, peripheral blood mononuclear cells, and HepG2 cells
evidence.exposure: Acute concentration-response experiments outside the body.
evidence.limitations: Direct mitochondrial inhibition in cells does not quantify clinical risk at a prescribed dose.
evidence.title: Cell-Permeable Succinate Rescues Mitochondrial Respiration in Cellular Models of Amiodarone Toxicity.

evidence.summary: Doxorubicin opened the mitochondrial permeability transition pore and caused mtDNA leakage in cardiomyocyte models; lower mitochondrial copy number increased susceptibility.
evidence.model: Patient PBMC correlation, isogenic human iPSC cardiomyocytes, and mice
evidence.exposure: Anthracycline-treated patients were correlated with biomarkers; causal tests used cell and mouse models.
evidence.limitations: The mechanistic experiments do not predict an individual patient's cardiotoxicity or safe dose.
evidence.title: Mitochondrial Amount Determines Doxorubicin-Induced Cardiotoxicity in Cardiomyocytes.

evidence.summary: Haloperidol caused time- and concentration-dependent complex I inhibition associated with thiol oxidation in incubated mouse brain slices.
evidence.model: Mouse brain slices incubated with haloperidol; isolated mitochondria used for reversal tests
evidence.exposure: In-vitro tissue exposure, including 10 nM haloperidol.
evidence.limitations: An isolated-tissue mechanism is not evidence of clinical mitochondrial injury at a prescribed dose.
evidence.title: Inhibition of mitochondrial complex I by haloperidol: the role of thiol oxidation.

evidence.summary: Acute and 28-day methylphenidate administration inhibited respiratory-chain complex activities in several brain regions of adult rats.
evidence.model: Adult rats after acute or once-daily administration for 28 days
evidence.exposure: Injected animal dosing; human exposure equivalence was not established in the abstract.
evidence.limitations: Rat brain enzyme activity cannot establish cognitive, neurological, or mitochondrial harm in treated people.
evidence.title: Inhibition of mitochondrial respiratory chain in the brain of adult rats after acute and chronic administration of methylphenidate.

evidence.summary: Simvastatin dose-dependently reduced respiratory-chain activity, membrane potential, and oxidative-phosphorylation efficiency in isolated rat brain mitochondria.
evidence.model: Mitochondria isolated from rat brain
evidence.exposure: Direct in-vitro statin exposure; no whole-body pharmacokinetics.
evidence.limitations: This demonstrates a laboratory mechanism, not CoQ10 depletion or clinical mitochondrial injury at prescribed doses.
evidence.title: Effects of Atorvastatin and Simvastatin on the Bioenergetic Function of Isolated Rat Brain Mitochondria.

evidence.summary: Atorvastatin dose-dependently reduced respiratory-chain activity, membrane potential, and oxidative-phosphorylation efficiency in isolated rat brain mitochondria.
evidence.model: Mitochondria isolated from rat brain
evidence.exposure: Direct in-vitro statin exposure; no whole-body pharmacokinetics.
evidence.limitations: This demonstrates a laboratory mechanism, not CoQ10 depletion or clinical mitochondrial injury at prescribed doses.
evidence.title: Effects of Atorvastatin and Simvastatin on the Bioenergetic Function of Isolated Rat Brain Mitochondria.

evidence.summary: In transgenic mice, acute oral metformin's glucose-lowering effect was attenuated when mitochondrial complex I inhibition was genetically bypassed.
evidence.model: Transgenic and control mice under standard-chow and high-fat-diet conditions
evidence.exposure: Acute oral metformin administration.
evidence.limitations: This supports a drug mechanism in mice; it does not show mitochondrial injury or settle every metformin mechanism in humans.
evidence.title: Metformin targets mitochondrial complex I to lower blood glucose levels.

evidence.summary: Berberine dose-dependently inhibited respiration through complex I in muscle cells and isolated muscle mitochondria, alongside AMPK activation.
evidence.model: L6 myotubes, isolated muscle mitochondria, and high-fat-fed rodents
evidence.exposure: Cell and isolated-mitochondria concentration responses; rodent efficacy used a more bioavailable derivative.
evidence.limitations: The study does not establish mitochondrial harm, benefit, or equivalent exposure from a person's supplement dose.
evidence.title: Berberine and its more biologically available derivative, dihydroberberine, inhibit mitochondrial respiratory complex I: a mechanism for the action of berberine to activate AMP-activated protein kinase and improve insulin action.

evidence.summary: A 16-week randomized trial in older adults reported improvements in measured mitochondrial fatty-acid oxidation with combined glycine plus N-acetylcysteine.
evidence.model: 24 older adults randomized to GlyNAC or alanine placebo, plus a young-adult reference group
evidence.exposure: Combined glycine and N-acetylcysteine for 16 weeks.
evidence.limitations: Small, specific population and combination intervention; effects cannot be assigned to glycine or NAC alone.
evidence.title: Supplementing Glycine and N-Acetylcysteine (GlyNAC) in Older Adults Improves Glutathione Deficiency, Oxidative Stress, Mitochondrial Dysfunction, Inflammation, Physical Function, and Aging Hallmarks: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

evidence.summary: In a randomized trial, urolithin A increased CD8+ T-cell fatty-acid oxidation capacity and secondary measures of mitochondrial biogenesis.
evidence.model: 50 healthy middle-aged adults randomized to urolithin A or placebo for 4 weeks
evidence.exposure: 1,000 mg urolithin A daily for 4 weeks.
evidence.limitations: Short study focused on immune-cell biology; it does not establish a broad clinical benefit or apply to every dose and population.
evidence.title: Effect of the mitophagy inducer urolithin A on age-related immune decline: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial.

evidence.summary: In a randomized trial, nicotinamide riboside did not change skeletal-muscle mitochondrial respiration, mitochondrial protein abundance, fractional area, or network morphology.
evidence.model: 40 middle-aged, obese, insulin-resistant men randomized to nicotinamide riboside or placebo
evidence.exposure: 1,000 mg nicotinamide riboside twice daily for 12 weeks.
evidence.limitations: This is a direct human null result in one male metabolic-risk population; it does not exclude effects in other tissues, doses, sexes, or populations.
evidence.title: Nicotinamide riboside does not alter mitochondrial respiration, content or morphology in skeletal muscle from obese and insulin-resistant men.

evidence.summary: A randomized crossover trial found no improvement in exercise outcomes, electron-transport-chain activities, or muscle mitochondrial biomarkers with resveratrol.
evidence.model: 11 adults with genetically verified mitochondrial myopathy
evidence.exposure: 1,000 mg resveratrol daily for 8 weeks versus placebo, separated by a 4-week washout.
evidence.limitations: This small disease-specific null trial does not address lower doses, longer use, or people without mitochondrial myopathy.
evidence.title: No effect of resveratrol in patients with mitochondrial myopathy: A cross-over randomized controlled trial.

evidence.summary: Dietary EPA plus DHA changed cardiac mitochondrial phospholipid composition and increased calcium capacity before permeability-transition-pore opening in rats.
evidence.model: Sham-operated and myocardial-infarction rats fed EPA plus DHA for 12 weeks
evidence.exposure: EPA plus DHA supplied as 2.3% of dietary energy for 12 weeks.
evidence.limitations: A rat cardiac-mitochondria result is not proof of a human clinical benefit from a particular fish-oil product or dose.
evidence.title: Dietary omega-3 fatty acids alter cardiac mitochondrial phospholipid composition and delay Ca2+-induced permeability transition.

evidence.summary: PQQ preserved mitochondrial number and increased PGC-1alpha and TFAM signaling in rotenone-injured Parkinson's disease models.
evidence.model: Rotenone-treated mice and rotenone-injured SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells
evidence.exposure: Injected PQQ at 0.8, 4, or 20 mg/kg/day in mice for 3 weeks, alongside rotenone.
evidence.limitations: A toxin-induced disease model does not establish mitochondrial or neurological benefit from oral PQQ in healthy people.
evidence.title: Pyrroloquinoline quinone promotes mitochondrial biogenesis in rotenone-induced Parkinson's disease model via AMPK activation.

evidence.summary: Ubiquinol improved skeletal-muscle oxidative-phosphorylation coupling efficiency, but did not improve exercise tolerance or oxygen-uptake kinetics.
evidence.model: 54 healthy, recreationally active men randomized to ubiquinol or placebo
evidence.exposure: 300 mg ubiquinol daily for 6 weeks.
evidence.limitations: The trial tested the reduced ubiquinol form in active men, was industry match-funded, and found no exercise-performance benefit; it should not be generalized to ubiquinone or other populations.
evidence.title: Effect of six weeks ubiquinol supplementation on mitochondrial respiratory function and exercise capacity in healthy males.

evidence.summary: CoQ10 did not change muscle CoQ10 content, mitochondrial respiratory function, reactive-oxygen-species production, or myalgia in simvastatin users.
evidence.model: 37 adults taking simvastatin, with or without myalgia, randomized to CoQ10 or placebo
evidence.exposure: 400 mg CoQ10 daily for 8 weeks.
evidence.limitations: This direct null result is limited to a small simvastatin-treated population and does not negate the separate ubiquinol finding in healthy active men.
evidence.title: Coenzyme Q10 Supplementation in Statin Treated Patients: A Double-Blinded Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial.

evidence.summary: MitoQ mildly lowered net mitochondrial hydrogen-peroxide levels during leak respiration and increased muscle catalase, but did not change mitochondrial respiration, density markers, or systemic oxidative-stress markers.
evidence.model: 20 healthy middle-aged men studied before and after MitoQ or CoQ10 supplementation
evidence.exposure: 20 mg MitoQ daily for 6 weeks.
evidence.limitations: Small male pre/post study without a placebo arm; lower mitochondrial hydrogen peroxide did not translate into improved mitochondrial respiration or systemic oxidative-stress measures.
evidence.title: MitoQ and CoQ10 supplementation mildly suppresses skeletal muscle mitochondrial hydrogen peroxide levels without impacting mitochondrial function in middle-aged men.

evidence.summary: In permeabilized human muscle, creatine increased sensitivity of mitochondrial respiration to ADP while phosphocreatine reduced it; 16 days of supplementation lowered basal leak respiration without changing ADP-stimulated respiration.
evidence.model: Permeabilized vastus-lateralis fibers from adults; 8 participants also completed supplementation
evidence.exposure: A 16-day creatine program; the dose is not reported in the PubMed abstract.
evidence.limitations: Small uncontrolled supplementation component and ex-vivo respiration measurements; this establishes phosphate-shuttle regulation, not a health or performance benefit.
evidence.title: The role of phosphorylcreatine and creatine in the regulation of mitochondrial respiration in human skeletal muscle.

evidence.summary: L-carnitine added to carbohydrate increased muscle carnitine and altered exercise fuel handling, with better matching of glycolytic, pyruvate-dehydrogenase, and mitochondrial flux at high intensity.
evidence.model: 14 healthy young men randomized to carbohydrate with or without L-carnitine
evidence.exposure: 2 g L-carnitine L-tartrate plus 80 g carbohydrate twice daily for 24 weeks; control received the same carbohydrate.
evidence.limitations: Small male study using 160 g/day carbohydrate to drive carnitine uptake; it does not establish the same effect from ordinary L-carnitine use, other forms, or shorter exposure.
evidence.title: Chronic oral ingestion of L-carnitine and carbohydrate increases muscle carnitine content and alters muscle fuel metabolism during exercise in humans.

evidence.summary: High-dose taurine increased taurine modification of mitochondrial tRNA in some patients and reduced recurrence of stroke-like episodes in MELAS.
evidence.model: 10 patients with recurrent stroke-like episodes from genetically defined MELAS
evidence.exposure: 9 or 12 g taurine daily for 52 weeks.
evidence.limitations: Tiny uncontrolled disease-specific trial at very high doses; it does not support mitochondrial or anti-aging benefit in people without MELAS.
evidence.title: Taurine supplementation for prevention of stroke-like episodes in MELAS: a multicentre, open-label, 52-week phase III trial.

evidence.summary: During riboflavin treatment, muscle complex I activity normalized in 3 of 4 retested patients with complex I-deficient mitochondrial myopathy, although clinical response was inconsistent.
evidence.model: 5 patients with mitochondrial myopathy and measured complex I deficiency
evidence.exposure: Riboflavin treatment; dose and duration are not reported in the PubMed abstract.
evidence.limitations: Very small uncontrolled case series in a specific diagnosed deficiency, with poor correlation between biochemical normalization and clinical improvement.
evidence.title: Treatment of complex I deficiency with riboflavin.

evidence.summary: Nine days of magnesium chloride modestly reduced fatty-acid-supported complex II respiration, maximal oxygen uptake, and sprint power in regular exercisers.
evidence.model: 15 magnesium-replete men and women who exercised regularly
evidence.exposure: 300 mg magnesium chloride twice daily for 9 days.
evidence.limitations: Small short study in magnesium-replete exercisers; it does not establish harm from dietary magnesium, correction of deficiency, longer use, or other supplemental forms.
evidence.title: Short-Term Magnesium Supplementation Has Modest Detrimental Effects on Cycle Ergometer Exercise Performance and Skeletal Muscle Mitochondria and Negligible Effects on the Gut Microbiota: A Randomized Crossover Clinical Trial.

evidence.summary: In acetaminophen-induced acute liver failure, circulating mitochondrial-DNA and glutamate-dehydrogenase damage markers were higher in nonsurvivors than survivors.
evidence.model: 69 patients with acetaminophen-induced acute liver failure: 34 survivors and 35 nonsurvivors
evidence.exposure: Acetaminophen overdose causing acute liver failure.
evidence.limitations: This is severe-overdose evidence only. It does not show mitochondrial injury from labeled therapeutic dosing and must not be presented as a routine-use warning.
evidence.title: Serum mitochondrial biomarkers and damage-associated molecular patterns are higher in acetaminophen overdose patients with poor outcome.

evidence.summary: Prolonged valproic-acid exposure reduced basal and maximal oxygen-consumption rates in primary human hepatocytes; a 3-hour exposure did not.
evidence.model: Primary human hepatocytes with short and prolonged valproic-acid exposure
evidence.exposure: Experimental exposure for 3 to 72 hours; the abstract does not establish equivalence to an individual's serum concentration.
evidence.limitations: A human-cell mechanism relevant to liver toxicity, not a clinical incidence estimate or proof of mitochondrial injury at a prescribed dose.
evidence.title: Valproic acid promotes mitochondrial dysfunction in primary human hepatocytes in vitro; impact of C/EBPalpha-controlled gene expression.

evidence.summary: Propofol directly inhibited fatty-acid oxidation and electron-transfer flux in human skeletal- and cardiac-muscle homogenates at concentrations achieved during anesthesia.
evidence.model: Skeletal muscle from 11 hip-surgery patients and myocardium from 10 organ donors, with rat tissue comparison
evidence.exposure: Acute ex-vivo propofol exposure from 2.5 to 100 micrograms/mL.
evidence.limitations: Tissue-homogenate mechanism, not a study of routine anesthesia outcomes or the incidence of propofol infusion syndrome.
evidence.title: Kinetic characteristics of propofol-induced inhibition of electron-transfer chain and fatty acid oxidation in human and rodent skeletal and cardiac muscles.

evidence.summary: In a prospective AIDS cohort, chronic zidovudine was associated with proximal myopathy and grossly enlarged muscle mitochondria that improved substantially after withdrawal.
evidence.model: 118 adults with AIDS followed for 1 year; 88 received zidovudine
evidence.exposure: 1,000-1,200 mg/day; myopathy occurred only after more than 270 days in this cohort.
evidence.limitations: Early-1990s high-dose regimen in people with AIDS; it does not estimate risk for current lower-dose combination therapy.
evidence.title: Mitochondrial myopathy associated with chronic zidovudine therapy in AIDS.

evidence.summary: Clinical gentamicin caused more mitochondria-dependent apoptosis than the C2b subtype in human iPSC-derived otic progenitor cells, with corresponding hearing-loss differences in mice.
evidence.model: Human iPSC-derived otic progenitor cells and mouse auditory-function models
evidence.exposure: Experimental exposure to clinical gentamicin mixture or purified gentamicin C2b.
evidence.limitations: A comparative formulation study in cells and mice; it does not quantify hearing-loss risk or mitochondrial injury in treated patients.
evidence.title: Establishment of a human inner ear model reveals that gentamicin C2b is substantially less ototoxic than clinical gentamicin.
